literature_notes: All three ledger lines (L1, L2, L3) describe the same construct: full-length human CLSTN1 with a 3xGGGGS linker fused to mNeonGreen or V5 at the protein C-terminus (after residue 981). Per the authoritative topology landmarks, residues 881–981 are intracellular; the C-terminal tag therefore faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface. Flow cytometry in L1/L3 was used to confirm overall expression levels of the lentiviral construct, not to demonstrate surface accessibility of the tag itself. No ledger line reports a tag insertion at an extracellular position of CLSTN1 (e.g., after the signal-peptide cleavage site at residue 28, or within the large extracellular domain 29–861). Because the sole evidence is an intracellular C-terminal fusion, zero extracellular surface tag sites qualify.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal 3xGGGGS-mNeonGreen/V5 fusion appended after the last residue (Y981) of full-length CLSTN1; the entire C-terminal domain (residues 881–981) is intracellular per topology, so this tag is cytoplasmic and not accessible on the extracellular face.
